title: Bug: Adaptive recovery during sanity_check_full when "var-log": "Resource limit matched" triggers reboot
author: peterbailey-arista
body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

High

### Description of the bug

Adaptive recovery will simply reboot the dut for `monit` sanity check failures, but for var-log disk space this  masks the true problem because

/etc/monit/conf.d/sonic-host contains the following:
```
check filesystem var-log with path /var/log
    if space usage > 90% for 10 times within 20 cycles then alert repeat every 1 cycles
```
and so on reboot the 10 times for 20 cycles must be repeated for monit to register the issue again 10 miniutes later.
Meaning the sanity check will seem stable without having recovered.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. run `df -h /var/log` to see the space used and available
2. run `sudo fallocate -l <XYZ>M /var/log/dummy.log` to fill more than 90% of the space
3. verify with `df -h /var/log` 

Do this before a test is running, wait 10 minutes.

4. run `sudo monit status rsyslog` to verify that monit is catching the problem
5. Now run the test and sanity check will spot the problem.

Some tests like linkflap stress tests on max topologies will sometimes fill up the var/log space as well but that is less reliable for reproducing.

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

Actual behaviour: dut reboots
Expected behaviour: var/log storage is recovered

comments.author: yxieca
comments.body:
Thanks for tackling the reboot-masking-on-full-`/var/log` case — the adaptive-recovery approach looks reasonable. A couple of questions before this goes in:

**1. `logrotate` target — snippet vs. main config.** The recovery runs:
```python
dut.shell("logrotate --force /etc/logrotate.d/rsyslog", module_ignore_errors=True)
```
`/etc/logrotate.d/rsyslog` is a fragment that's `include`d by `/etc/logrotate.conf` (it's rendered at runtime by `logrotate-config.sh`). Invoking `logrotate` directly on the fragment skips the global directives in `/etc/logrotate.conf` (rotate count, and the tmpfs state file under `/dev/shm/logrotate/`). Was running the fragment directly intentional, or would `logrotate -f /etc/logrotate.conf` better match how SONiC normally rotates and be more robust across branches? (If the fragment is deliberate, a one-line comment explaining why would help future readers.)

**2. Exact-string match on the monit status.** The branch keys off:
```python
if services_status.get('var-log') == 'Resource limit matched':
```
`services_status['var-log']` comes from `get_monit_services_status()`, which takes the text after `status` on that service's line in `sudo monit status`. Have we confirmed that value is exactly `Resource limit matched` on all supported branches/monit versions (no trailing qualifier, no localization/version drift)? If the string ever differs, `_recover_monit` silently falls through to `action = 'reboot'`, which reintroduces the reboot this PR is trying to avoid. Would a `startswith`/substring check (grounded against the actual monit output) be safer here?

Not blocking on my end — just want to make sure the recovery actually frees space and reliably triggers so it doesn't quietly regress to reboot.

*Reviewed by AI agent on behalf of Ying.*
